old_caption: The video captures a serene scene dominated by a thick layer of fog that blankets the landscape. The fog is dense and billows gently, creating a dynamic and ever-changing atmosphere. In the upper left corner, the branches of leafless trees are visible, suggesting it might be late autumn or winter. On the right side, the tops of lush green trees stand out against the foggy backdrop, adding contrast to the scene. The fog's movement is subtle but noticeable, with patches occasionally clearing to reveal glimpses of the sky and the trees beneath. The overall mood is tranquil and mysterious, evoking a sense of calm and quietude. There are no animals or characters present in the video; the focus remains solely on the natural elements and their interplay with the fog. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to fully absorb the peaceful and ethereal beauty of the scene.

caption: The video captures a hazy, low-contrast scene dominated by a swirling gray-blue mist that fills most of the view. Bare brownish branches hang along the top edge, while dark green leafy tree silhouettes crowd the right side and lower-right corner. A small pale point appears near the center-right and slowly drifts downward through the haze. The mist churns continuously, its darker and lighter patches slowly drifting and deforming across the view. This internal reshaping alters the clouded texture while the surrounding branches and trees remain largely in place. The point's descent is slight but steady, with only a small sideways shift against the moving haze. The overall layout remains broadly steady as the haze continues its quiet turbulence. No obvious expansion occurs; the visible change is confined to the soft reshaping of the smoky region and the slow movement of the pale point.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
